title: Mammals Mute Robo, and Also Clear It

scenes.tts: Comm has been found only in some insects. So how does a mammalian axon stay deaf until it crosses?
scenes.visual: Title card: Mammals Mute Robo, and Also Clear It. A mouse spinal cord section, a commissural axon approaching the floor plate.
scenes.narration: Comm has been found only in some insects. So how does a mammalian axon stay deaf until it crosses?

scenes.tts: The fly has one slit gene. Mice have three, and two conventional Robo receptors, Robo one and Robo two.
scenes.caption: The fly has one slit gene. Mice have three, and two conventional Robo receptors, Robo1 and Robo2.
scenes.visual: On screen: fly, one slit gene; mouse, Slit1, Slit2, Slit3, and a growth cone with Robo1 and Robo2.
scenes.narration: The fly has one slit gene. Mice have three, and two conventional Robo receptors, Robo1 and Robo2.

scenes.tts: Earlier work found that mice lacking Slit one and Slit two had no defect in commissural axon guidance.
scenes.caption: Earlier work found that mice lacking Slit1 and Slit2 had no defect in commissural axon guidance.
scenes.visual: Normal crossing in a Slit1 and Slit2 double mutant.
scenes.narration: Earlier work found that mice lacking Slit1 and Slit2 had no defect in commissural axon guidance.

scenes.tts: In 2004, researchers removed all three. Use the three questions. What should the axons do?
scenes.visual: All three Slit genes crossed out. Names on screen: Long, Tessier-Lavigne and colleagues, 2004. The three questions appear briefly.
scenes.narration: In 2004, researchers removed all three. Use the three questions. What should the axons do?

scenes.tts: With no Slit, there is no Slit push, though other cues remain. The axons still reach the midline, drawn by netrin.
scenes.visual: Axons reach the floor plate.
scenes.narration: With no Slit, there is no Slit push, though other cues remain. The axons still reach the midline, drawn by netrin.

scenes.tts: Many stalled in the floor plate. Others crossed and then turned back.
scenes.visual: Some axons stop inside the floor plate; others cross and loop back. Small fly slit and robo ladders appear beside them for comparison.
scenes.narration: Many stalled in the floor plate. Others crossed and then turned back.

scenes.tts: Next, a culture experiment. Zou and colleagues grew pieces of embryonic rat spinal cord, called explants, in a gel.
scenes.visual: Two explants cut from a spinal cord and set in a collagen gel. Label: explants.
scenes.narration: Next, a culture experiment. Zou and colleagues grew pieces of embryonic rat spinal cord, called explants, in a gel.

scenes.tts: Dorsal explants gave axons that had not yet crossed. Explants that kept the floor plate gave axons that had crossed.
scenes.visual: Left: dorsal explant, precrossing axons growing out (netrin added). Right: explant with its floor plate, postcrossing axons growing out.
scenes.narration: Dorsal explants gave axons that had not yet crossed. Explants that kept the floor plate gave axons that had crossed.

scenes.tts: Each kind sat beside cells releasing Slit two. Which axons should Slit affect?
scenes.visual: Both explants beside a clump of Slit2-releasing cells. Question marks over both.
scenes.narration: Each kind sat beside cells releasing Slit2. Which axons should Slit affect?
scenes.caption: Each kind sat beside cells releasing Slit2. Which axons should Slit affect?

scenes.tts: Slit two held back the growth of axons that had crossed. Axons that had not crossed were not held back.
scenes.visual: Left dish: precrossing axons grow normally beside Slit2 cells. Right dish: postcrossing axons grow much less near the Slit2 cells.
scenes.narration: Slit2 held back the growth of axons that had crossed. Axons that had not crossed were not held back.
scenes.caption: Slit2 held back the growth of axons that had crossed. Axons that had not crossed were not held back.

scenes.tts: These were different axons, not one axon before and after. Still, crossing goes with a change in the response to Slit.
scenes.visual: The two dishes side by side. Label: different axons; response differs with crossing.
scenes.narration: These were different axons, not one axon before and after. Still, crossing goes with a change in the response to Slit.

scenes.tts: So what keeps a mammalian axon deaf before it crosses? An unusual member of the Robo family, called Robo three.
scenes.caption: So what keeps a mammalian axon deaf before it crosses? An unusual member of the Robo family, called Robo3.
scenes.visual: A growth cone with an odd receptor among Robo1 and Robo2. Label: Robo3, also called Rig-1.
scenes.narration: So what keeps a mammalian axon deaf before it crosses? An unusual member of the Robo family, called Robo3.

scenes.tts: In 2004, it was found on commissural axons before they cross.
scenes.visual: Names and year on screen: Sabatier, Tessier-Lavigne and colleagues, 2004. Robo3 on the precrossing segment of the axon only.
scenes.narration: In 2004, it was found on commissural axons before they cross.

scenes.tts: Remove Robo three from a mouse. Slit is present. Robo one and Robo two are still made. Predict.
scenes.caption: Remove Robo3 from a mouse. Slit is present. Robo1 and Robo2 are still made. Predict.
scenes.visual: Robo3 crossed out. Question mark at the floor plate.
scenes.narration: Remove Robo3 from a mouse. Slit is present. Robo1 and Robo2 are still made. Predict.

scenes.tts: Almost no commissural axons cross. They approach the floor plate and turn away. They hear Slit too early.
scenes.visual: Axons approach the floor plate and turn along their own side.
scenes.narration: Almost no commissural axons cross. They approach the floor plate and turn away. They hear Slit too early.

scenes.tts: That resembles the fly comm mutant.
scenes.visual: The fly comm ladder beside the mouse section.
scenes.narration: That resembles the fly comm mutant.

scenes.tts: But Robo three does not clear Robo one and Robo two from the surface. It blunts their response while they stay in the membrane.
scenes.caption: But Robo3 does not clear Robo1 and Robo2 from the surface. It blunts their response while they stay in the membrane.
scenes.visual: Robo1 and Robo2 stay on the membrane; Robo3 drawn as a hand over their ears. Small label: a cartoon of the effect, not a known contact.
scenes.narration: But Robo3 does not clear Robo1 and Robo2 from the surface. It blunts their response while they stay in the membrane.

scenes.tts: Comm lowers Robo one by sorting, and in at least one other way. Robo three mutes it.
scenes.caption: Comm lowers Robo1 by sorting, and in at least one other way. Robo3 mutes it.
scenes.visual: Split screen: fly, receptor sent to lysosome; mouse, receptor muted on the surface.
scenes.narration: Comm lowers Robo1 by sorting, and in at least one other way. Robo3 mutes it.

scenes.tts: Mammals also clear some Robo one. Proteins called en-dee-fip one and two send it to be degraded before crossing.
scenes.caption: Mammals also clear some Robo1. Proteins called Ndfip1 and Ndfip2 send it to be degraded before crossing.
scenes.visual: Mouse neuron: some new Robo1 diverted to an endosome for degradation, labelled Ndfip1/2. Beside it, Robo3 muting the Robo1 that reaches the surface.
scenes.narration: Mammals also clear some Robo1. Proteins called Ndfip1 and Ndfip2 send it to be degraded before crossing.

scenes.tts: Two splice forms of Robo three matter here. In mouse, the form present before crossing disappears afterwards.
scenes.caption: Two splice forms of Robo3 matter here. In mouse, the form present before crossing disappears afterwards.
scenes.visual: Robo3.1 on the precrossing segment, gone after the floor plate.
scenes.narration: Two splice forms of Robo3 matter here. In mouse, the form present before crossing disappears afterwards.

scenes.tts: A second form appears on crossed axons and helps keep them from recrossing.
scenes.visual: Robo3.2 appears on the postcrossing segment.
scenes.narration: A second form appears on crossed axons and helps keep them from recrossing.

scenes.tts: Mammalian Robo three has a second job too. It works with the netrin receptor DCC and strengthens netrin attraction.
scenes.caption: Mammalian Robo3 has a second job too. It works with the netrin receptor DCC and strengthens netrin attraction.
scenes.visual: Robo3 beside DCC; the netrin pull arrow thickens.
scenes.narration: Mammalian Robo3 has a second job too. It works with the netrin receptor DCC and strengthens netrin attraction.

scenes.tts: The same gene matters in people. Mutations in human Robo three cause horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis.
scenes.caption: The same gene matters in people. Mutations in human Robo3 cause horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis.
scenes.visual: Simple line drawing of two eyes that cannot turn sideways, and a curved spine. No patient imagery.
scenes.narration: The same gene matters in people. Mutations in human Robo3 cause horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis.

scenes.tts: In patients, motor and sensory pathways that normally cross in the brainstem appear uncrossed.
scenes.visual: Brainstem diagram: pathways that should cross stay on their own side.
scenes.narration: In patients, motor and sensory pathways that normally cross in the brainstem appear uncrossed.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: mammals both mute their Robo receptors and clear some of them, until the axon has crossed.
scenes.visual: Summary card: flies, Comm limits Robo1 through sorting and another inhibitory activity; mammals, Robo3 mutes Robo1 and Robo2, and Ndfips also clear some Robo1.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: mammals both mute their Robo receptors and clear some of them, until the axon has crossed.
